title: SOCIAL BIAS FRAMES: Reasoning about Social and Power Implications of Language
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, Social Bias Inference Corpus (SBIC), measures the ability of models to detect and explain pragmatic implications of social bias against various demographic groups. For religion, it specifically measures the detection of stereotypes and harmful implications, such as the stereotype that 'Muslims are all terrorists' implied by certain statements.
models_tested: SBF-GPT1 (a fine-tuned version of OpenAI's GPT)
SBF-GPT2 (a fine-tuned version of OpenAI's GPT-2)
findings: Religion/culture is one of the top three most represented categories of bias in the collected dataset. The models tested struggle to generate relevant and nuanced social bias inferences related to religious groups. For instance, when presented with a post about a Muslim political group, the model tended to generate a generic stereotype ('muslims are terrorists') rather than the more specific, entailed implications from the text.
